q: 她跳舞___得很漂亮，朋友们都爱看。
zh: 她跳舞跳得很漂亮，朋友们都爱看。
py: tā tiào wǔ tiào de hěn piào liang péng you men dōu ài kàn
en: She dances beautifully, and her friends all love watching her.
why: 跳舞 is the verb 跳 plus the object 舞, so 得 cannot follow it directly. Repeat 跳 first: 跳舞跳得很漂亮. Writing 舞 again would hang 得 on a noun.

q: 我朋友做饭___得很好吃，周末常请我们去他家。
zh: 我朋友做饭做得很好吃，周末常请我们去他家。
py: wǒ péng you zuò fàn zuò de hěn hǎo chī zhōu mò cháng qǐng wǒ men qù tā jiā
en: My friend cooks really well, and often invites us to his home on weekends.
why: 做饭 already carries the object 饭, so the verb is repeated before 得: 做饭做得很好吃. 吃 or 饭 would not be the verb that 得 describes.

q: 下雨天他开车___得特别慢，我们到得很晚。
zh: 下雨天他开车开得特别慢，我们到得很晚。
py: xià yǔ tiān tā kāi chē kāi de tè bié màn wǒ men dào de hěn wǎn
en: On rainy days he drives especially slowly, so we arrive very late.
why: 开车 is verb + object, so the verb 开 is said again before 得. 了 cannot go between the verb and 得, and 车 would put 得 after a noun.

q: 我朋友唱歌___得不错，聚会上大家都请她唱。
zh: 我朋友唱歌唱得不错，聚会上大家都请她唱。
py: wǒ péng you chàng gē chàng de bù cuò jù huì shàng dà jiā dōu qǐng tā chàng
en: My friend sings pretty well, so everyone asks her to sing at parties.
why: After 唱歌 the verb must be repeated: 唱歌唱得不错. Repeating the object 歌 or adding 很 before 得 does not give 得 the verb it needs to attach to.

q: 昨天的聚会，小李说话___得太多了，大家都不想听了。
zh: 昨天的聚会，小李说话说得太多了，大家都不想听了。
py: zuó tiān de jù huì xiǎo lǐ shuō huà shuō de tài duō le dà jiā dōu bù xiǎng tīng le
en: At yesterday’s party Xiao Li talked too much, and nobody wanted to listen any more.
why: 说话 is verb + object, so repeat 说 before 得: 说话说得太多了. 话得 puts 得 after an object, and 听 is not the verb just used.

q: 朋友们约我周末去爬山，可是我爬山___得很慢，怕拖累大家。
zh: 朋友们约我周末去爬山，可是我爬山爬得很慢，怕拖累大家。
py: péng you men yuē wǒ zhōu mò qù pá shān kě shì wǒ pá shān pá de hěn màn pà tuō lèi dà jiā
en: My friends invited me to go hiking this weekend, but I climb slowly and I am afraid of holding everyone back.
why: 爬山 is a verb-object word; the first character is repeated before 得: 爬山爬得很慢. 山 or 去 cannot carry 得, which must touch the verb being judged.

q: 她写字写___很整齐，朋友们都爱看她的笔记。
zh: 她写字写得很整齐，朋友们都爱看她的笔记。
py: tā xiě zì xiě de hěn zhěng qí péng you men dōu ài kàn tā de bǐ jì
en: She writes very neatly, and her friends all like to read her notes.
why: The repeated verb 写 is followed directly by 得, then the comment 很整齐. 地 belongs before a verb, and 了 or 着 cannot link a verb to its comment.

q: 冬天他滑雪___得特别好，我们都想跟他学。
zh: 冬天他滑雪滑得特别好，我们都想跟他学。
py: dōng tiān tā huá xuě huá de tè bié hǎo wǒ men dōu xiǎng gēn tā xué
en: He skis especially well in winter, and we all want to learn from him.
why: 滑雪 is verb + object, so 滑 comes back before 得: 滑雪滑得特别好. The other choices are not the verb that 得 describes, and 雪得 would attach 得 to a noun.

q: 我姐姐吃饭___得很慢，每次都是最后一个吃完。
zh: 我姐姐吃饭吃得很慢，每次都是最后一个吃完。
py: wǒ jiě jie chī fàn chī de hěn màn měi cì dōu shì zuì hòu yī gè chī wán
en: My older sister eats slowly, and she is always the last to finish.
why: With the object 饭 in the sentence, 得 must come after a second 吃: 吃饭吃得很慢. Putting 得 straight after 饭 is the classic mistake.

q: 这个周末的聚会，他喝酒___得有点多，所以我们送他回家了。
zh: 这个周末的聚会，他喝酒喝得有点多，所以我们送他回家了。
py: zhè gè zhōu mò de jù huì tā hē jiǔ hē de yǒu diǎn duō suǒ yǐ wǒ men sòng tā huí jiā le
en: At this weekend’s party he drank a bit too much, so we took him home.
why: 喝酒 has its own object, so 喝 is said again before 得: 喝酒喝得有点多. 了 cannot stand between the verb and 得, and 酒得 puts 得 after a noun.

q: 秋天爸爸骑车___得很快，我跟不上。
zh: 秋天爸爸骑车骑得很快，我跟不上。
py: qiū tiān bà ba qí chē qí de hěn kuài wǒ gēn bù shàng
en: In autumn my dad rides fast and I cannot keep up.
why: 骑车 = verb + object, so 骑 is repeated: 骑车骑得很快. Without the second 骑, 得 would follow the noun 车, which is wrong.

q: 今天的饭他___得很好吃，朋友们都夸他。
zh: 今天的饭他做得很好吃，朋友们都夸他。
py: jīn tiān de fàn tā zuò de hěn hǎo chī péng you men dōu kuā tā
en: He cooked today’s meal really well, and his friends all praised him.
why: The object 今天的饭 is already in front, so only the bare verb 做 stands before 得. 做饭 would repeat the object, and 吃 is not what he did.

q: 这辆车他___得特别稳，我们都很放心。
zh: 这辆车他开得特别稳，我们都很放心。
py: zhè liàng chē tā kāi de tè bié wěn wǒ men dōu hěn fàng xīn
en: He drives this car very steadily, so we feel safe with him.
why: With 车 moved to the front, one verb 开 is left before 得: 这辆车他开得特别稳. 开车 would say the object a second time and breaks the pattern.

q: 她的字___得很漂亮，朋友们都夸她。
zh: 她的字写得很漂亮，朋友们都夸她。
py: tā de zì xiě de hěn piào liang péng you men dōu kuā tā
en: She writes beautifully, and her friends all praise her.
why: The object 字 is fronted (她的字), leaving the bare verb 写 right before 得. 写字得 would put 得 after an object, the classic error.

q: 这首歌小李___得特别好听，大家都鼓掌了。
zh: 这首歌小李唱得特别好听，大家都鼓掌了。
py: zhè shǒu gē xiǎo lǐ chàng de tè bié hǎo tīng dà jiā dōu gǔ zhǎng le
en: Xiao Li sang this song really well, and everyone applauded.
why: 这首歌 is fronted as the object, so only the verb 唱 stands before 得. 唱歌 would repeat an object, and 听 is not what Xiao Li did.

q: 他___说得很流利，朋友们都很佩服他。
zh: 他中文说得很流利，朋友们都很佩服他。
py: tā zhōng wén shuō de hěn liú lì péng you men dōu hěn pèi fú tā
en: He speaks Chinese fluently, and his friends admire him.
why: Moving the object between subject and verb gives 他中文说得很流利. 中文的 makes it a possessive noun without a proper link, and 把 does not belong in this pattern.

q: 周末的聚会，菜她___得太咸了，大家都没吃多少。
zh: 周末的聚会，菜她做得太咸了，大家都没吃多少。
py: zhōu mò de jù huì cài tā zuò de tài xián le dà jiā dōu méi chī duō shǎo
en: At the weekend party she made the dishes too salty, so people ate very little.
why: 菜 is fronted, so a single verb 做 sits before 得. Repeating 做菜 would double the object, and 吃 is not the action being judged.

q: 春游的照片她___得特别好，朋友们都想让她多拍几张。
zh: 春游的照片她拍得特别好，朋友们都想让她多拍几张。
py: chūn yóu de zhào piàn tā pāi de tè bié hǎo péng you men dōu xiǎng ràng tā duō pāi jǐ zhāng
en: She took the spring-outing photos especially well, and her friends want her to take more.
why: The object 春游的照片 is fronted, so the verb 拍 comes straight before 得. 拍照 would add an object again, which can never precede 得.

q: 他唱歌唱得___好，朋友们不想听。
zh: 他唱歌唱得不好，朋友们不想听。
py: tā chàng gē chàng de bù hǎo péng you men bù xiǎng tīng
en: He doesn’t sing well, and his friends don’t want to listen.
why: Negate the comment after 得: 唱得不好. 没 negates a past event, not a quality here, and the other choices are not negatives for an adjective.

q: 昨晚太吵了，我睡___太好。
zh: 昨晚太吵了，我睡得不太好。
py: zuó wǎn tài chǎo le wǒ shuì de bù tài hǎo
en: It was too noisy last night, and I did not sleep very well.
why: 不 goes after 得, on the adjective: 睡得不太好. 不得 or 没得 put the negative between verb and 得, where nothing can stand.

q: 他今天骑车骑得___快，因为风很大。
zh: 他今天骑车骑得不快，因为风很大。
py: tā jīn tiān qí chē qí de bù kuài yīn wèi fēng hěn dà
en: He didn’t ride fast today because of the strong wind.
why: The adjective after 得 is negated with 不: 骑得不快. 没 would point to a past event and cannot negate 快 in this pattern.

q: 周末下雨，我们玩得___太开心。
zh: 周末下雨，我们玩得不太开心。
py: zhōu mò xià yǔ wǒ men wán de bù tài kāi xīn
en: It rained at the weekend, so we did not have a very good time.
why: To say the comment is not true, put 不 right after 得: 玩得不太开心, even though the time is past. 很 cannot stack in front of 太, and 非 and 别 do not negate an adjective.

q: 昨晚太热，我睡得___怎么好。
zh: 昨晚太热，我睡得不怎么好。
py: zuó wǎn tài rè wǒ shuì de bù zěn me hǎo
en: It was too hot last night and I did not sleep very well.
why: 不怎么 softens a negative comment and follows 得: 睡得不怎么好. 很怎么 is not a phrase, and 没 does not combine with 怎么 here.

q: 春天的天气变化大，我们爬山爬得___太顺利，下午还下雨了。
zh: 春天的天气变化大，我们爬山爬得不太顺利，下午还下雨了。
py: chūn tiān de tiān qì biàn huà dà wǒ men pá shān pá de bù tài shùn lì xià wǔ hái xià yǔ le
en: The spring weather changes a lot, so our climb did not go very smoothly, and in the afternoon it rained.
why: Negation sits after 得, in front of 太顺利: 爬得不太顺利. 未 is a written-style negative, 别 is only for commands, and 很 cannot stand in front of 太.

q: 他昨天喝得___多，所以今天没事。
zh: 他昨天喝得不多，所以今天没事。
py: tā zuó tiān hē de bù duō suǒ yǐ jīn tiān méi shì
en: He did not drink much yesterday, so he is fine today.
why: Use 不 after 得 for a comment that does not hold: 喝得不多. 没 or 没有 would negate the drinking itself, which is not the idea.

q: 夏天我们游泳游得___好，所以不敢去深水。
zh: 夏天我们游泳游得不好，所以不敢去深水。
py: xià tiān wǒ men yóu yǒng yóu de bù hǎo suǒ yǐ bù gǎn qù shēn shuǐ
en: We do not swim well, so in summer we do not dare to go into deep water.
why: The adjective is negated: 游得不好. 不是 must be followed by a noun phrase, not a bare adjective, so it does not fit here.

q: 那几天天气不好，大家玩得___怎么开心。
zh: 那几天天气不好，大家玩得不怎么开心。
py: nà jǐ tiān tiān qì bù hǎo dà jiā wán de bù zěn me kāi xīn
en: The weather was bad those days, so nobody had a very good time.
why: 不怎么 goes after 得 and before the adjective: 玩得不怎么开心. 未 is written style, 别 is only for commands, and 很怎么 is not a phrase.

q: 周末的聚会你玩得___？
zh: 周末的聚会你玩得怎么样？
py: zhōu mò de jù huì nǐ wán de zěn me yàng
en: How was the party this weekend for you?
why: 怎么样 asks about the part after 得 and is already a question word, so 吗 must not follow it. 很怎么样 and a bare 怎么 do not form a question here.

q: 你昨晚睡得好___？
zh: 你昨晚睡得好吗？
py: nǐ zuó wǎn shuì de hǎo ma
en: Did you sleep well last night?
why: A yes/no question about the comment is 睡得好吗？ 怎么样 would stack a second question word, and 很 cannot go before 吗.

q: 他中文说得___不___？
zh: 他中文说得好不好？
py: tā zhōng wén shuō de hǎo bù hǎo
en: Does he speak Chinese well?
why: The A-not-A question repeats the bare adjective: 好不好. 很 cannot stay inside an A-not-A, and the adjective must be identical on both sides.

q: 这次春游你们玩___怎么样？
zh: 这次春游你们玩得怎么样？
py: zhè cì chūn yóu nǐ men wán de zěn me yàng
en: How was the spring outing for you all?
why: Ask about the comment after the verb: 玩得怎么样. 地 would modify a following verb, and 着 or 过 cannot link a verb to 怎么样.

q: 春游那天，你们起得早___早？
zh: 春游那天，你们起得早不早？
py: chūn yóu nà tiān nǐ men qǐ de zǎo bù zǎo
en: Did you get up early on the day of the outing?
why: A-not-A asks about the adjective after 得: 早不早. 吗 and 很 cannot be used inside it, and 没 does not form an A-not-A on a bare adjective.

q: 这次考试你考得___吗？
zh: 这次考试你考得好吗？
py: zhè cì kǎo shì nǐ kǎo de hǎo ma
en: Did you do well on this exam?
why: 吗 needs a plain statement: 考得好吗. 怎么样 and 好不好 are already questions, and 很好不好 is wrong twice over.

q: 你觉得这次春游安排得___？
zh: 你觉得这次春游安排得怎么样？
py: nǐ jué de zhè cì chūn yóu ān pái de zěn me yàng
en: How do you think this spring outing was organised?
why: To ask for an opinion about the outing, put 怎么样 after 得 with nothing after it. 吗 cannot be added to a question word.

q: 你们昨天玩得开心___？
zh: 你们昨天玩得开心吗？
py: nǐ men zuó tiān wán de kāi xīn ma
en: Did you have fun yesterday?
why: 玩得开心 is a statement and 吗 turns it into a yes/no question. 怎么样, 什么 and 几 would be a second question word with 开心 already given.

q: 夏天的中午热___很，我不想出去。
zh: 夏天的中午热得很，我不想出去。
py: xià tiān de zhōng wǔ rè de hěn wǒ bù xiǎng chū qù
en: It is really hot at noon in summer, and I do not want to go out.
why: 热得很 needs 得 to link the adjective to 很. 地 only goes before verbs, and 了 or 着 cannot give the intensifying meaning here.

q: 今天冷___要命，我们别去爬山了。
zh: 今天冷得要命，我们别去爬山了。
py: jīn tiān lěng de yào mìng wǒ men bié qù pá shān le
en: It is freezing today, so let us not go hiking.
why: 要命 needs 得 after the adjective: 冷得要命. 了 would make it a change of state without the meaning of extreme degree, and 地 only goes before verbs.

q: 我今天累___，不想出去玩了。
zh: 我今天累死了，不想出去玩了。
py: wǒ jīn tiān lèi sǐ le bù xiǎng chū qù wán le
en: I am dead tired today and no longer want to go out.
why: 死了 attaches directly to the adjective: 累死了. 得 is not used before 死了, and 很 plus 死了 is never said.

q: 听说他们要来，我高兴___不得了。
zh: 听说他们要来，我高兴得不得了。
py: tīng shuō tā men yào lái wǒ gāo xīng de bù dé liǎo
en: When I heard they were coming, I was overjoyed.
why: 不得了 follows an adjective with 得: 高兴得不得了. 死 cannot join 不得了, and 地 or 了 would not link the adjective to the degree.

q: 今天___热得很，我们在家吃西瓜吧。
zh: 今天热得很，我们在家吃西瓜吧。
py: jīn tiān rè de hěn wǒ men zài jiā chī xī guā ba
en: It is really hot today, so let us eat watermelon at home.
why: 热得很 already means very hot, so no degree word goes before the adjective. 很热得很 or 真热得很 doubles the intensifier.

q: 春天了，可是山上还是冷___，大家都穿着厚外套。
zh: 春天了，可是山上还是冷得很，大家都穿着厚外套。
py: chūn tiān le kě shì shān shàng hái shì lěng de hěn dà jiā dōu chuān zhe hòu wài tào
en: It is spring, but it is still very cold on the mountain, and everyone is wearing a thick coat.
why: Adjective + 得很 gives strong degree. 冷很 lacks the 得, and 冷极 needs 了 and no 得. A bare 冷得 is incomplete.

q: 那个周末的聚会热闹___，大家都玩到很晚。
zh: 那个周末的聚会热闹极了，大家都玩到很晚。
py: nà gè zhōu mò de jù huì rè nao jí le dà jiā dōu wán dào hěn wǎn
en: That weekend’s party was extremely lively, and everyone played until late.
why: 极了 attaches to the adjective directly: 热闹极了. 得极了 and 极得 are not Chinese, and 很 cannot stack with 极了.

q: 朋友们都说那家店的菜好吃___，周末我们打算一起去尝尝。
zh: 朋友们都说那家店的菜好吃得很，周末我们打算一起去尝尝。
py: péng you men dōu shuō nà jiā diàn de cài hǎo chī de hěn zhōu mò wǒ men dǎ suàn yī qǐ qù cháng cháng
en: My friends all say the food at that restaurant is really delicious, so we plan to try it together this weekend.
why: 好吃得很 is adjective + 得 + 很. 好吃很 drops 得, and 极得 reverses the fixed pattern 极了, which takes no 得.

q: 他高兴___对我说：“周末见！”
zh: 他高兴地对我说：“周末见！”
py: tā gāo xīng de duì wǒ shuō zhōu mò jiàn
en: He said to me happily, “See you at the weekend!”
why: 高兴 describes how he spoke and stands before the verb 说, so it takes 地. 得 would need a verb right in front of it, and 了 or 着 are not manner markers.

q: 朋友们笑___很开心。
zh: 朋友们笑得很开心。
py: péng you men xiào de hěn kāi xīn
en: My friends laughed with great joy.
why: 笑 is followed by a comment on how they laughed, so 笑得很开心. 地 goes before a verb, and 了 or 着 do not introduce a comment.

q: 孩子们开心___在雪地里跑来跑去。
zh: 孩子们开心地在雪地里跑来跑去。
py: hái zi men kāi xīn de zài xuě dì lǐ pǎo lái pǎo qù
en: The children happily ran around in the snow.
why: 开心 modifies the action 跑来跑去 and comes before it, so use 地. 得 belongs after a verb, and 过 or 着 cannot link an adjective to a verb.

q: 他今天起___那么早，是想先去买下午聚会用的东西。
zh: 他今天起得那么早，是想先去买下午聚会用的东西。
py: tā jīn tiān qǐ de nà me zǎo shì xiǎng xiān qù mǎi xià wǔ jù huì yòng de dōng xi
en: He got up that early today because he wanted to buy things for the afternoon party first.
why: Timing after the verb is a comment, so 起得那么早. 地 would put an adjective before a verb, which does not describe how early.

q: 我朋友很聪明，学___也很快。
zh: 我朋友很聪明，学得也很快。
py: wǒ péng you hěn cōng ming xué de yě hěn kuài
en: My friend is very clever and learns fast too.
why: 很聪明 describes him; how he learns needs the verb with 得: 学得也很快. 地 before the verb or 了 cannot give this meaning.

q: 她的歌___很好听，大家都爱听。
zh: 她的歌唱得很好听，大家都爱听。
py: tā de gē chàng de hěn hǎo tīng dà jiā dōu ài tīng
en: Her singing sounds very good, and everyone loves to listen.
why: To say the singing sounds good, the verb 唱 must carry 得: 她的歌唱得很好听. 唱很好听 lacks the link, and 很 or 好 alone is not a sentence.

q: 昨天的雪下___很大，路上没有人。
zh: 昨天的雪下得很大，路上没有人。
py: zuó tiān de xuě xià de hěn dà lù shàng méi yǒu rén
en: The snow was heavy yesterday, and there was nobody on the road.
why: How heavy the snow fell is a comment on 下, so 下得很大. 了 cannot sit between the verb and its comment, and 地 would go before a verb.

q: 春天的花开___很早，今年二月就开了。
zh: 春天的花开得很早，今年二月就开了。
py: chūn tiān de huā kāi de hěn zǎo jīn nián èr yuè jiù kāi le
en: The spring flowers bloomed very early; they were already out in February this year.
why: The timing of the blooming is a comment, so 开得很早. 地 modifies a following verb, and 着 or 过 cannot take such a comment.

q: 朋友们昨天到___太早了，我还没起床。
zh: 朋友们昨天到得太早了，我还没起床。
py: péng you men zuó tiān dào de tài zǎo le wǒ hái méi qǐ chuáng
en: My friends arrived too early yesterday and I was not even up yet.
why: 到得太早了 evaluates how early they arrived: verb + 得 + 太 + adjective, with 了 at the end. 着 and 过 cannot link a verb to such a comment.

q: 这个冬天过___特别快，转眼就是春天了。
zh: 这个冬天过得特别快，转眼就是春天了。
py: zhè gè dōng tiān guò de tè bié kuài zhuǎn yǎn jiù shì chūn tiān le
en: This winter went by especially fast, and spring is suddenly here.
why: How fast the winter passed is a comment, so 过得特别快. 了 may not come between 过 and the comment, and 地 goes before a verb.

q: 雨下___越来越大，我们只好取消了周末的野餐。
zh: 雨下得越来越大，我们只好取消了周末的野餐。
py: yǔ xià de yuè lái yuè dà wǒ men zhǐ hǎo qǔ xiāo le zhōu mò de yě cān
en: The rain kept getting heavier, so we had to cancel the weekend picnic.
why: The rain’s intensity is a comment after 下, so 下得越来越大. 着 and 了 cannot sit between a verb and a comment, and 地 goes before a verb.

q: 小李昨天走___很慢，因为路很滑。
zh: 小李昨天走得很慢，因为路很滑。
py: xiǎo lǐ zuó tiān zǒu de hěn màn yīn wèi lù hěn huá
en: Xiao Li walked slowly yesterday because the road was slippery.
why: How slowly he walked is a comment on 走, so 走得很慢. 地 cannot follow a verb and 了 cannot link a verb to a comment.

zh: 夏天我弟弟游泳游得很快。
py: xià tiān wǒ dì di yóu yǒng yóu de hěn kuài
en: In summer my little brother swims fast.
why: 游泳 is verb + object, so 游 is repeated before 得. The time word may sit before or after the subject, but 得 must touch the second 游.

zh: 我朋友中文说得很流利。
py: wǒ péng you zhōng wén shuō de hěn liú lì
en: My friend speaks Chinese fluently.
why: The object 中文 moves before the verb, leaving 说 right before 得. A fronted object may also start the sentence, but nothing may follow the adjective.

zh: 昨晚我睡得不好。
py: zuó wǎn wǒ shuì de bù hǎo
en: I did not sleep well last night.
why: 不 goes after 得 in front of the adjective: 睡得不好. 昨晚 may go before or after the subject.

zh: 你们春游玩得怎么样？
py: nǐ men chūn yóu wán de zěn me yàng
en: How was the spring outing for you all?
why: Ask about the comment with 怎么样 after 得. 春游 can come before or after 你们 as the topic, and 怎么样 has no 吗.

zh: 今天冷得要命。
py: jīn tiān lěng de yào mìng
en: It is freezing today.
why: 要命 follows an adjective through 得: 冷得要命. Putting 得 after 要命 or leaving it out breaks the pattern.

zh: 孩子们开心地在雪地里玩。
py: hái zi men kāi xīn de zài xuě dì lǐ wán
en: The children play happily in the snow.
why: 开心地 describes the manner of playing, so it stands before the verb. After 玩 it would need 得 and a comment instead.

zh: 他很高，跑得也很快。
py: tā hěn gāo pǎo de yě hěn kuài
en: He is tall, and he also runs fast.
why: Two comments: 他很高 describes him, and 跑得也很快 describes how he runs. The verb 跑 must come before 得.

zh: 下雪天爸爸开车开得特别小心。
py: xià xuě tiān bà ba kāi chē kāi de tè bié xiǎo xīn
en: On snowy days Dad drives very carefully.
why: 开车 is verb + object, so 开 is said again before 得: 开车开得特别小心. The time phrase can be before or after the subject.

zh: 这些照片她拍得特别好，大家都想看。
py: zhè xiē zhào piàn tā pāi de tè bié hǎo dà jiā dōu xiǎng kàn
en: She took these photos especially well, and everyone wants to see them.
why: The object 这些照片 is fronted, so 拍 stands right before 得. Either the object or the subject can come first.

zh: 昨天天气不好，我们玩得不太开心。
py: zuó tiān tiān qì bù hǎo wǒ men wán de bù tài kāi xīn
en: The weather was bad yesterday, so we did not have a very good time.
why: The negative 不太 stays on the adjective after 得: 玩得不太开心. Placing 不 before 玩 would negate the verb itself.

zh: 你昨晚睡得好吗？
py: nǐ zuó wǎn shuì de hǎo ma
en: Did you sleep well last night?
why: The yes/no question is built on the comment: 睡得好吗. 昨晚 can come before or after 你, but 得 must touch 睡.

zh: 下雪了，孩子们高兴得不得了。
py: xià xuě le hái zi men gāo xīng de bù dé liǎo
en: It snowed, and the children are overjoyed.
why: 不得了 follows an adjective through 得: 高兴得不得了. Without 得, 不得了 cannot attach.

zh: 她唱歌唱得非常好听。
py: tā chàng gē chàng de fēi cháng hǎo tīng
en: She sings very beautifully.
why: 唱歌 is verb + object, so 唱 is repeated before 得: 唱歌唱得非常好听. The 得 must stay on the second 唱.

zh: 他着急地给朋友打电话。
py: tā zháo jí de gěi péng you dǎ diàn huà
en: He anxiously phoned his friend.
why: 着急地 describes the manner in which he phoned, so it comes before 打电话. A comment after the verb would need 得 instead.

zh: 小李饺子包得很好。
py: xiǎo lǐ jiǎo zi bāo de hěn hǎo
en: Xiao Li wraps dumplings very well.
why: The object 饺子 moves in front of 包, and 得很好 follows the verb. Subject and object can swap places at the start.

src_py: wǒ dì di tiào wǔ hěn hǎo
task: Rewrite with 得 and repeat the verb.
zh: 我弟弟跳舞跳得很好。
py: wǒ dì di tiào wǔ tiào de hěn hǎo
en: My little brother dances well.
why: 跳舞 is verb + object, so after repeating 跳, 得 and the comment follow: 跳舞跳得很好. Without the second 跳, 得 would follow a noun.

src: 我朋友做菜做得很好吃。
src_py: wǒ péng you zuò cài zuò de hěn hǎo chī
task: Move the object before the verb instead of repeating it.
zh: 我朋友菜做得很好吃。
py: wǒ péng you cài zuò de hěn hǎo chī
en: My friend cooks really well.
why: The object 菜 jumps in front of 做, so the repeated verb disappears. 菜 may also start the sentence, but nothing may follow the adjective.

src_py: tā zuó tiān shuì de hěn hǎo
zh: 他昨天睡得不好。
py: tā zuó tiān shuì de bù hǎo
en: He did not sleep well yesterday.
why: To negate the comment, replace 很好 with 不好 after 得. The past time does not allow 没 before 睡.

src_py: tā tiào wǔ tiào de hěn hǎo
task: Say he does not dance well.
zh: 他跳舞跳得不好。
py: tā tiào wǔ tiào de bù hǎo
en: He does not dance well.
why: Negate only the adjective: 跳舞跳得不好. 不 before 跳 or 没 would negate the dancing itself and break the pattern.

src_py: nǐ men zuó tiān wán de hěn kāi xīn
task: Turn it into an A-not-A question.
zh: 你们昨天玩得开心不开心？
py: nǐ men zuó tiān wán de kāi xīn bù kāi xīn
en: Did you have fun yesterday?
why: The A-not-A is built on the adjective: 开心不开心. The 很 disappears, and 吗 is not added.

src_py: nǐ zuó tiān kǎo de hěn hǎo
task: Ask about it with 怎么样.
zh: 你昨天考得怎么样？
py: nǐ zuó tiān kǎo de zěn me yàng
en: How did your exam go yesterday?
why: 怎么样 takes the place of 很好 after 得 and works as the question word, so 吗 must not be added.

task: Say it is freezing with 得要命.
zh: 今天冷得要命。
py: jīn tiān lěng de yào mìng
en: It is freezing today.
why: 得要命 replaces 很: the adjective 冷 is followed by 得 and 要命, and 很 must not stay in front.

src_py: péng you yào lái wǒ hěn gāo xīng
task: Say you are extremely happy using 得不得了.
zh: 朋友要来，我高兴得不得了。
py: péng you yào lái wǒ gāo xīng de bù dé liǎo
en: My friend is coming, and I am overjoyed.
why: The degree word 很 is replaced by 得不得了 after the adjective: 高兴得不得了. 很 cannot be kept in front.

src_py: tā xiào de hěn kāi xīn
task: Say he smiled happily, with the manner before the verb.
zh: 他开心地笑了。
py: tā kāi xīn de xiào le
en: He smiled happily.
why: 开心地 stands before the verb and describes the manner of smiling; the comment 得很开心 after the verb is replaced by 地 before it.

src_py: tā rèn zhēn de tīng péng you shuō huà
task: Say how attentively she listened, with 得 after the verb.
zh: 她听朋友说话听得很认真。
py: tā tīng péng you shuō huà tīng de hěn rèn zhēn
en: She listens to her friends very attentively.
why: To comment on how she listened, repeat 听 after the object phrase and attach 得: 听朋友说话听得很认真. The 地 goes away with the move.

s: 昨天的雪下了得很大。
s_py: zuó tiān de xuě xià le de hěn dà
zh: 昨天的雪下得很大。
py: zuó tiān de xuě xià de hěn dà
en: The snow was heavy yesterday.
why: Nothing may sit between 下 and 得, not even 了. 昨天 already shows the past, so 下得很大 is right.

s: 她跳舞得很漂亮，朋友们都爱看。
s_py: tā tiào wǔ de hěn piào liang péng you men dōu ài kàn
zh: 她跳舞跳得很漂亮，朋友们都爱看。
py: tā tiào wǔ tiào de hěn piào liang péng you men dōu ài kàn
en: She dances beautifully, and her friends all love watching her.
why: 得 must follow a verb, not the object 舞. Repeat the verb: 跳舞跳得很漂亮.

s: 昨晚太吵了，我没睡得好。
s_py: zuó wǎn tài chǎo le wǒ méi shuì de hǎo
zh: 昨晚太吵了，我睡得不好。
py: zuó wǎn tài chǎo le wǒ shuì de bù hǎo
en: It was too noisy last night, so I did not sleep well.
why: The negative belongs after 得: 睡得不好. 没 before the verb cannot combine with 得, even in the past.

s: 朋友们不玩得开心。
s_py: péng you men bù wán de kāi xīn
zh: 朋友们玩得不开心。
py: péng you men wán de bù kāi xīn
en: My friends did not have a good time.
why: 不 negates the comment, so it sits after 得 on the adjective: 玩得不开心. 不玩得开心 is not Chinese.

s: 你们春游玩得怎么样吗？
s_py: nǐ men chūn yóu wán de zěn me yàng ma
zh: 你们春游玩得怎么样？
py: nǐ men chūn yóu wán de zěn me yàng
en: How was the spring outing for you all?
why: 怎么样 already asks the question, so 吗 cannot be added.

s: 你觉得他中文说得很好不好？
s_py: nǐ jué de tā zhōng wén shuō de hěn hǎo bù hǎo
zh: 你觉得他中文说得好不好？
py: nǐ jué de tā zhōng wén shuō de hǎo bù hǎo
en: Do you think he speaks Chinese well?
why: Inside an A-not-A question the adjective is bare: 好不好. 很 cannot stay.

s: 他听说朋友要来，高兴不得了。
s_py: tā tīng shuō péng you yào lái gāo xīng bù dé liǎo
zh: 他听说朋友要来，高兴得不得了。
py: tā tīng shuō péng you yào lái gāo xīng de bù dé liǎo
en: When he heard his friend was coming he was overjoyed.
why: 不得了 needs 得 after the adjective: 高兴得不得了. Dropping 得 is the typical error.

s: 他说地很清楚，朋友们都听懂了。
s_py: tā shuō de hěn qīng chu péng you men dōu tīng dǒng le
zh: 他说得很清楚，朋友们都听懂了。
py: tā shuō de hěn qīng chu péng you men dōu tīng dǒng le
en: He spoke very clearly, and his friends all understood.
why: A comment after the verb takes 得, not 地. 地 only marks a manner word before a verb.

s: 我朋友很漂亮写字，大家都喜欢看。
s_py: wǒ péng you hěn piào liang xiě zì dà jiā dōu xǐ huan kàn
zh: 我朋友写字写得很漂亮，大家都喜欢看。
py: wǒ péng you xiě zì xiě de hěn piào liang dà jiā dōu xǐ huan kàn
en: My friend writes beautifully, and everyone likes to look at it.
why: In Chinese the verb comes first and the adjective follows 得: 写字写得很漂亮. English-style adjective-before-verb is wrong.

s: 他来地很早，朋友们还没到。
s_py: tā lái de hěn zǎo péng you men hái méi dào
zh: 他来得很早，朋友们还没到。
py: tā lái de hěn zǎo péng you men hái méi dào
en: He came early, and his friends have not arrived yet.
why: Timing like 很早 is a comment after the verb, linked by 得. 地 only marks a manner word before a verb, so 来地很早 is wrong.

s: 我弟弟踢得很好足球，朋友们都想和他一组。
s_py: wǒ dì di tī de hěn hǎo zú qiú péng you men dōu xiǎng hé tā yī zǔ
zh: 我弟弟足球踢得很好，朋友们都想和他一组。
py: wǒ dì di zú qiú tī de hěn hǎo péng you men dōu xiǎng hé tā yī zǔ
en: My little brother plays football very well, and his friends all want to be on his team.
why: The object 足球 cannot follow the comment. Move it before the verb: 足球踢得很好.

s: 昨天的雨下得不大，我们还是去爬山了。
zh: 昨天的雨下得不大，我们还是去爬山了。
py: zuó tiān de yǔ xià de bù dà wǒ men hái shì qù pá shān le
en: Yesterday’s rain was not heavy, so we still went hiking.
why: Correct: 不 follows 得. The past time does not call for 没, which tempts learners to reject it.

s: 他踢足球踢得好，但是游泳游得不好。
zh: 他踢足球踢得好，但是游泳游得不好。
py: tā tī zú qiú tī de hǎo dàn shì yóu yǒng yóu de bù hǎo
en: He plays football well, but he does not swim well.
why: Correct. A bare adjective after 得 is fine in a contrast, and both verb-object phrases repeat their verb before 得.

s: 冬天的太阳落得很早，下午五点天就黑了。
zh: 冬天的太阳落得很早，下午五点天就黑了。
py: dōng tiān de tài yang luò de hěn zǎo xià wǔ wǔ diǎn tiān jiù hēi le
en: In winter the sun sets very early; it is dark by five in the afternoon.
why: Correct: how early the sun sets is a comment after the verb 落, linked by 得. There is no 了 between them.

s: 你们昨天的聚会开得怎么样？
zh: 你们昨天的聚会开得怎么样？
py: nǐ men zuó tiān de jù huì kāi de zěn me yàng
en: How was your party yesterday?
why: Correct: 怎么样 follows 得 and needs no 吗. The past time does not change anything.

s: 他今天的心情好得很，一直在笑。
zh: 他今天的心情好得很，一直在笑。
py: tā jīn tiān de xīn qíng hǎo de hěn yī zhí zài xiào
en: He is in a really good mood today and keeps smiling.
why: Correct: adjective + 得很, with no 很 in front.

s: 今年夏天热极了，晚上也睡不着。
zh: 今年夏天热极了，晚上也睡不着。
py: jīn nián xià tiān rè jí le wǎn shàng yě shuì bù zháo
en: This summer is extremely hot, and I cannot sleep at night either.
why: Correct: 极了 attaches directly with no 得, which tempts learners to add 得.

s: 她高兴地对朋友说：“周末我请客！”
zh: 她高兴地对朋友说：“周末我请客！”
py: tā gāo xīng de duì péng you shuō zhōu mò wǒ qǐng kè
en: She said happily to her friends, “It is my treat this weekend!”
why: Correct: 高兴 describes how she spoke and stands before the verb, so 地 is right. 得 would be wrong here.

s: 他跑步很快，朋友们都比不过他。
zh: 他跑步很快，朋友们都比不过他。
py: tā pǎo bù hěn kuài péng you men dōu bǐ bù guò tā
en: He is fast at running, and none of his friends can beat him.
why: Correct: an activity as topic plus 很 + adjective is accepted in Chinese. It need not take 得.

s: 她做饭做得不太好，所以朋友们带来了蛋糕。
zh: 她做饭做得不太好，所以朋友们带来了蛋糕。
py: tā zuò fàn zuò de bù tài hǎo suǒ yǐ péng you men dài lái le dàn gāo
en: She does not cook very well, so her friends brought a cake.
why: Correct: the verb 做 is repeated, 得 follows it, and 不太 sits on the adjective.
